finding: Complete paired trajectories plus raw utterances cannot identify a latent intervention partition when language is reducible to the environment/intervention index; an exact invertible reparameterization changes intervention support from two latent variables to one while preserving all observed data and index-derived language.

counterexample.model_a: Z=(A,B), intervention flips both A and B
counterexample.model_b: C=A, D=A xor B, same intervention flips only C
counterexample.observed_equivalence: identical complete pre/post observations under an absorbed invertible observation map
counterexample.language_condition: L is generated only from environment index E
counterexample.consequence: sigma(X,E,L)=sigma(X,E), so language cannot refine the causal equivalence class

prior_art_added: heterogeneous measurement-model identifiability for binary latent causal graphs
surviving_claim: Only language relations not measurable from the environment/intervention index may qualify; they must remove a specific trajectory-level causal symmetry and be supported by independently separating intervention effects.
adoption_blockers: novelty beyond auxiliary-variable, multi-view, hidden-regime, mechanistic-independence, and measurement-model identifiability not established
R0.1 public capability baseline not reproduced
